p.src: After seeing Granny Liu off, Zhou Rui’s wife went upstairs to report to Lady Wang. But Lady Wang was not in her rooms; when she asked the maids, she learned that Lady Wang had gone to Aunt Xue’s for a leisurely chat. On hearing this, Zhou Rui’s wife went back out through the eastern corner gate, crossed into the east compound, and made her way to Pear Fragrance Court. Just as she reached the courtyard gate, she saw Lady Wang’s maid Jinchuan’er playing on the sloping steps with a little girl whose hair had only recently been allowed to grow. Seeing Zhou Rui’s wife approach, they knew she had something to report and pointed their lips toward the room within.

p.src: Zhou Rui’s wife gently lifted the curtain and entered, where she found Lady Wang and Aunt Xue deep in a long conversation about household affairs, social obligations, and the like. Not daring to interrupt them, she went into the inner room. There she saw Xue Baochai in informal dress, her hair loosely gathered in a simple knot, sitting at the inner end of the kang and leaning over its little table as she traced embroidery patterns with her maid Ying’er. When she saw her come in, Baochai put down her brush, turned around, and invited her with a beaming smile: “Sit down, Sister Zhou.” Zhou Rui’s wife hastened to smile in return and asked, “Are you well, miss?” As she sat down on the edge of the kang, she continued, “I haven’t seen you come over to our side for the past two or three days. Surely Master Bao hasn’t offended you?” Baochai laughed. “Nothing of the kind. It is only that my old ailment has flared up again, so I haven’t left my room these past two days.” “Just so,” said Zhou Rui’s wife. “But what is the underlying cause of your illness? You ought to summon a physician while there is still time, have him write a proper prescription, and faithfully take several doses so that you can root it out once and for all. It is no laughing matter for someone so young to be left with the root of a chronic illness.” At this Baochai laughed. “Please, don’t mention medicine again. I cannot tell you how much silver we have wasted on doctors and medicines for this illness. No famous physician or miraculous remedy ever produced the slightest effect. Later, fortunately, there came a bald-headed monk who claimed to specialize in illnesses with no known name, so we asked him to examine me. He said mine was a hot poison carried from the womb; luckily my constitution was naturally strong, so it was not serious, but ordinary medicines would be of no use. He then prescribed a rare secret remedy and gave us a packet of medicinal powder to serve as its catalyst; it had the strangest fragrance. I have no idea where he obtained it. He said that whenever the illness flared up, taking one pill would cure it. Strangely enough, his medicine really does have some effect.”

p.src: Zhou Rui’s wife asked, “What sort of rare prescription is it? If you tell us, miss, we can remember it and pass it on; should anyone suffer from the same illness, it would be a charitable deed.” Asked this, Baochai smiled. “You are better off never using this prescription. If you do, its fussiness will be the death of you. The ingredients themselves all have fixed amounts; the only difficulty lies in the words ‘by happy chance.’ You need twelve liang of stamens from white peonies blooming in spring, twelve liang from white lotuses blooming in summer, twelve liang from white hibiscus flowers in autumn, and twelve liang from white plum blossoms in winter. On the Spring Equinox of the following year, these four kinds of stamens must be dried in the sun, mixed with the medicinal powder, and ground together. Then you need twelve qian of rainwater collected on the day of Rain Water—” Zhou Rui’s wife hastily exclaimed, “Good heavens! By that reckoning, it would take three years! And what if no rain falls at all on the day of Rain Water?” Baochai laughed. “That is why I said such timely rain is so hard to come by. If it does not rain, there is nothing to do but wait again. You also need twelve qian of dew from the day of White Dew, twelve qian of frost from the day of Frost’s Descent, and twelve qian of snow from the day of Light Snow. Mix these four kinds of water evenly, blend them with the medicine, add twelve qian of honey and twelve qian of white sugar, roll the mixture into pills the size of longans, place them in an old porcelain jar, and bury it beneath the roots of a flowering plant. Whenever the illness flares up, take out one pill and swallow it with a decoction made from twelve fen of phellodendron bark.”

p.src: Zhou Rui’s wife laughed when she heard this. “Amitabha! What a recipe to torment a person to death! You could wait ten years without all those happy chances coming together.” “As it happened,” said Baochai, “within a year or two after he gave us the prescription, we chanced to obtain everything, and after great difficulty managed to prepare one batch. We brought it north with us from the south, and it is now buried beneath a pear tree.” Zhou Rui’s wife asked again, “Does this medicine have a name?” “Yes,” said Baochai. The scabby-headed monk named it too. It is called ‘Cold Fragrance Pill.’” Zhou Rui’s wife nodded, then asked, “What exactly do you feel when the illness comes on?” “Nothing very much,” replied Baochai. “I merely wheeze and cough a little. Once I take a pill, I feel better.”

p.src: Zhou Rui’s wife was about to say more when she suddenly heard Lady Wang ask, “Who is in the room?” Zhou Rui’s wife hurried out to answer and took the opportunity to report the matter concerning Granny Liu. She waited a short while; when Lady Wang said nothing further, she was just about to withdraw when Aunt Xue suddenly said with a smile, “Wait a moment. I have something for you to take with you.” With that, she called for Xiangling. The curtain rustled, and in came the little maid who had just been playing with Jinchuan’er. “What do you want me for, madam?” she asked. “Bring me the flowers from the box,” said Aunt Xue. Xiangling acknowledged the order, went over to the other side, and returned carrying a small brocade box. Aunt Xue said, “These are a new fashion from the palace—twelve flowers made of gathered gauze. Yesterday it occurred to me that it would be a pity to leave them lying unused, so why not give them to the young ladies to wear? I meant to send them yesterday but happened to forget. Your arrival today is most timely, so take them with you. Give each of your household’s three young ladies a pair; of the remaining six, send two to Miss Lin and give the other four to Sister Feng.” Lady Wang said, “Keep them for Baochai to wear. Why trouble yourself thinking of the others?” Aunt Xue replied, “You do not know, sister. Baochai is an odd girl—she has never cared for flowers or face powder.”

p.src: As she spoke, Zhou Rui’s wife took the box and left the room, where she found Jinchuan still basking in the sun. Zhou Rui’s wife asked her, “Is that young maid Xiangling the girl they often say was bought on the way to the capital—the one over whom a murder case arose?” “Who else could it be?” replied Jinchuan. While they were speaking, Xiangling came over with a beaming smile. Zhou Rui’s wife took her by the hand and studied her closely for a while, then said to Jinchuan with a smile, “What a pretty girl! She even has something of young Mistress Rong’s manner over at the Eastern Mansion.” Jinchuan laughed. “That’s just what I say too.” Zhou Rui’s wife then asked Xiangling, “How old were you when you entered service here?” Then she asked, “Where are your parents now? How old are you this year? Where are you originally from?” To every question Xiangling merely shook her head and said, “I don’t remember.” Hearing this, Zhou Rui’s wife and Jinchuan could only sigh and grieve for her awhile.

p.src: Before long, Zhou Rui’s wife carried the flowers to the rear of Lady Wang’s principal apartments. It happened that Grandmother Jia had lately remarked that there were too many granddaughters crowded together and that it was inconvenient. She had kept only Baoyu and Daiyu near her for company, while moving Yingchun, Tanchun, and Xichun into the three small rear rooms behind Lady Wang’s quarters, with Li Wan to accompany and look after them. As this lay on her way, Zhou Rui’s wife came here first. She saw several young maids waiting in the rear rooms to be summoned. Yingchun’s maid Siqi and Tanchun’s maid Daishu were just lifting the curtain to come out, each carrying a teacup. Zhou Rui’s wife knew at once that the sisters were sitting together. Entering the inner room, she found Yingchun and Tanchun playing Go by the window. Zhou Rui’s wife presented the flowers and explained why she had brought them. The two promptly stopped their game, rose slightly to thank her, and told their maids to put the flowers away.

p.src: Zhou Rui’s wife acknowledged them, then said, “The Fourth Young Lady isn’t in her room. I expect she’s over with the Old Lady.” The maids said, “Isn’t that the Fourth Young Lady in the other room?” On hearing this, Zhou Rui’s wife went over to that room. There she found Xichun playing with Zhineng, a young nun from Water Moon Convent. When Xichun saw Zhou Rui’s wife come in, she asked what had brought her. Zhou Rui’s wife opened the flower box and explained the reason for her visit. Xichun laughed. “I was just telling Zhineng that tomorrow I’ll shave my head and become a nun with her. And now, of all times, you bring me flowers! If I shave my head, where am I supposed to wear them?” At this they all joked for a while, and Xichun called her maid Ruhua to take the flowers.

p.src: Zhou Rui’s wife then asked Zhineng, “When did you arrive? And where has that bald old nuisance of a mistress of yours gone?” Zhineng replied, “We came early this morning. After my mistress had seen Her Ladyship, she went to Lord Yu’s residence and told me to wait for her here.” Zhou Rui’s wife asked again, “Have you received the monthly allowance for incense offerings due on the fifteenth?” Zhineng shook her head. “I don’t know.” Hearing this, Xichun asked Zhou Rui’s wife, “Who manages the monthly allowances for the temples now?” “Yu Xin manages them,” replied Zhou Rui’s wife. Xichun laughed. “That explains it. As soon as her mistress arrived, Yu Xin’s wife hurried over and whispered with her for ages. I expect that was what they were discussing.”

p.src: After chatting with Zhineng a little longer, Zhou Rui’s wife set off for Xifeng’s quarters. She passed along the narrow passage beneath Li Wan’s rear window and, through the glass, saw Li Wan reclining asleep on the kang. Continuing past the western flower wall, she went out through the west corner gate and entered Xifeng’s courtyard. When she reached the main room, she saw the young maid Feng’er sitting on the threshold of Xifeng’s chamber. At the sight of Zhou Rui’s wife, Feng’er quickly waved her toward the eastern room. Understanding the hint, Zhou Rui’s wife tiptoed into the eastern room, where she found the nurse patting little Dajie to sleep. In a whisper, Zhou Rui’s wife asked the nurse, “Is the young lady taking her afternoon nap? Surely it’s time she woke.” The nurse shook her head. As they spoke, a burst of laughter came from the other side, and among it could be heard Jia Lian’s voice. Then a door sounded, and Ping’er emerged carrying a large brass basin and told Feng’er to ladle some water and take it inside. Ping’er then came over. As soon as she saw Zhou Rui’s wife, she asked, “What brings you running here again, auntie?” Zhou Rui’s wife quickly rose, handed her the box, and explained about the flowers. On hearing this, Ping’er opened the box, took out four sprigs, and went back inside. After a short while, she came out with two of them in her hand and first called Caiming over with the instruction, “Take these to the mansion across the way for young Mistress Rong to wear.” Only then did she tell Zhou Rui’s wife to return and convey Xifeng’s thanks.

p.src: Only then did Zhou Rui’s wife set off for Grandmother Jia’s quarters. As she passed through the entrance hall, she looked up and unexpectedly saw her daughter, all dressed up and just arrived from her husband’s family. Zhou Rui’s wife hurriedly asked, “What brings you here at this hour?” Her daughter smiled. “Mother, have you been well lately? I waited at home for half the day, but you never came out. What has kept you so busy that you haven’t come home? I grew tired of waiting, so I came ahead, paid my respects to the Old Lady, and am now going to pay my respects to Madam. What errands do you still have unfinished, Mother, and what are you carrying?” Zhou Rui’s wife laughed. “Oh! Of all days, Granny Liu had to come today. I meddled in her affairs and spent half the day running about for her; then Her Ladyship happened to see me and sent me to deliver these flowers to the young ladies and mistresses. Even now I haven’t finished delivering them all. You would not have come here now unless something had happened.” Her daughter smiled. “You really are a good guesser, Mother. To tell you the truth, your son-in-law drank a few cups too many the other day and quarreled with someone. Somehow the man maliciously accused him of having no clear place of origin and reported him to the authorities, who intend to escort him back to his native district. So I came to consult you: whom might we ask to use their influence and settle the matter?” On hearing this, Zhou Rui’s wife said, “I knew it would be something like that. What is there to make such a fuss about? Go home and wait for me. As soon as I have delivered Miss Lin’s flowers, I will come home. Madam and Second Mistress are both occupied just now, so go home and wait for me. It is nothing serious. Why be in such a panic?” Her daughter turned to leave, but added, “Mother, do come quickly, whatever you do.” “All right,” said Zhou Rui’s wife. Young people like you have never been through anything; no wonder you become so anxious.” With that, she went to Daiyu’s room.

p.src: As it happened, Daiyu was not in her own room but in Baoyu’s, where everyone was amusing themselves with a set of linked rings. Zhou Rui’s wife entered and said with a smile, “Miss Lin, Her Ladyship asked me to bring you these flowers to wear.” Hearing this, Baoyu immediately asked, “What sort of flowers? Let me see them.” Even as he spoke, he had already reached out and taken them. When he opened the box, he found ingenious artificial flowers made in the palace style from layered gauze. Daiyu merely glanced at them in Baoyu’s hand and asked, “Were these sent only to me, or did all the other young ladies receive some too?” “Everyone has received hers,” replied Zhou Rui’s wife. “These two are yours.” Daiyu gave a cold laugh. “I knew it. I never receive anything unless it is what the others have left over.” Zhou Rui’s wife heard her but said not a word. Baoyu then asked, “Sister Zhou, what took you over there?” Zhou Rui’s wife explained, “Madam was there, so I went to report to her. Her Ladyship then asked me to bring these along while I was about it.” Baoyu asked, “What is Sister Bao doing at home? Why hasn’t she come over these past few days?” “She has not been feeling very well,” replied Zhou Rui’s wife. On hearing this, Baoyu said to the maids, “Will one of you go and inquire after her? Say that Miss Lin and I have sent you to pay our respects to Her Ladyship and Sister Bao, and ask what illness Sister Bao has and what medicine she is taking. Properly speaking, I ought to go myself, but explain that I have just returned from school and caught a slight chill, and that I shall visit her in person another day.” At this, Qianxue answered that she would go. Zhou Rui’s wife then went on her way, and nothing further need be said of it. Now Zhou Rui’s son-in-law was none other than Leng Zixing, Yucun’s friend. He had recently become embroiled in a lawsuit over the sale of antiques, which was why he had sent his wife to seek a favor. Relying on her masters’ power and influence, Zhou Rui’s wife thought little of such matters. All she need do was ask Xifeng that evening, and it would be settled. Zhou Rui’s wife entered and said with a smile, “Miss Lin, Her Ladyship asked me to bring you these flowers to wear.”
Hearing this, Baoyu immediately asked, “What sort of flowers?
Let me see them.”
Even as he spoke, he had already reached out and taken them.
When he opened the box, he found ingenious artificial flowers made in the palace style from layered gauze.
Daiyu merely glanced at them in Baoyu’s hand and asked, “Were these sent only to me, or did all the other young ladies receive some too?”
“Everyone has received hers,” replied Zhou Rui’s wife. “These two are yours.”

Zhou Rui’s wife heard her but said not a word.

p.src: The next day, after washing and dressing, Xifeng first reported to Lady Wang and then went to take leave of Grandmother Jia. When Baoyu heard of it, he too wanted to go along for the outing. Xifeng had no choice but to agree. She waited while he changed his clothes, and then the pair rode in a carriage and soon entered the Ning mansion. Jia Zhen’s wife, Lady You, and Jia Rong’s wife, Lady Qin, the mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, were already waiting and led a host of concubines, maids, and married servants out beyond the ceremonial gate to welcome them. As soon as Lady You saw Xifeng, she teased her laughingly for a while, as was her custom; then, taking Baoyu by the hand, she led them into the main room and seated them. After Lady Qin had served tea, Xifeng said, “Why did you invite me here? If you have anything fine to offer me, bring it out at once. I still have business to attend to.” Before Lady You or Lady Qin could reply, several concubines standing below laughed and said, “It would have been another matter had Second Mistress not come today, but now that you are here, you cannot have your own way.” As they were speaking, Jia Rong came in to pay his respects. Baoyu asked, “Is Elder Brother not at home today?” Lady You replied, “He has gone outside the city to pay his respects to his father. You must be terribly bored. What are you doing sitting here? Why don’t you go and amuse yourself too?”

p.src: Qin-shi smiled and said, “What fortunate timing! That younger brother of mine whom Uncle Baoyu was so eager to meet last time is here today. I believe he is in the study. Why don’t you go and see him, Uncle?” At this, Baoyu immediately climbed down from the kang to go. Lady You and Xifeng both hurriedly said, “Take care! What is the rush?” At the same time, they ordered the attendants to follow him with the utmost care and not let him suffer the least discomfort; merely having accompanied the Old Lady there was by no means the end of their responsibility. Xifeng said, “If that is so, why not invite young Master Qin in and let me have a look at him too? Am I somehow unfit to meet him?” Lady You laughed. “No, no! You needn’t meet him. He is not like the children of our family, who are accustomed to rough-and-tumble ways. Other people’s children are used to being quiet and refined. If he suddenly met a scapegrace like you, he might laugh himself to death.” Xifeng laughed. “It is enough that I refrain from laughing at everyone else under heaven. Am I to let a mere child laugh at me?” Jia Rong laughed. “That isn’t what she means. He is naturally bashful and has never seen such grand company. If you meet him, Aunt, you may only end up annoyed.” Xifeng said, “Whatever he is like, I insist on seeing him! Stop talking your damned nonsense. If you don’t bring him for me to see at once, I’ll give you a good slapping.” Jia Rong said with a grin, “I wouldn’t dare defy you. I’ll bring him here.”

p.src: With that, he went out and, sure enough, brought in a young lad. He was a little slimmer than Baoyu, with delicate brows and clear eyes, a fair face and crimson lips. Handsome in figure and graceful in manner, he seemed even finer than Baoyu; only he was timid and shy, with something maidenly about him. Blushing and tongue-tied, he slowly bowed to Xifeng and paid his respects. Delighted, Xifeng first gave Baoyu a playful shove and laughed, “He has outdone you!” Then she leaned forward, took the boy by the hand, and made him sit beside her. At her leisure she asked how old he was, what books he was studying, how many brothers he had, and what formal name he had been given. Qin Zhong answered each question in turn. Xifeng’s maids and married serving women had already noticed that, since this was her first meeting with Qin Zhong, she had not brought a suitable introductory gift; they therefore hurried over to the other side to inform Pinger. Pinger knew that Xifeng and Qin-shi were very close, and that even though he was only a young lad, the gift must not be too meager. Acting on her own judgment, she took a length of cloth and two small gold ingots stamped “First Place in the Palace Examination,” and gave them to the messenger to deliver. Even then, Xifeng laughed and said the gifts were far too slight. Qin-shi and the others thanked her. After the meal, Lady You, Xifeng, Qin-shi, and the others played dominoes, but that need not detain us.

p.src: From the moment Baoyu saw how exceptional Qin Zhong was, he felt as though something were missing within him. He remained dazed for a long while, and then one of his foolish notions arose as he thought, “Can such a person truly exist in this world! Beside him, I now see that I am nothing but a filthy pig and a mangy cur. How hateful that I was born into a princely house of rank and splendor! Had I too been born into the family of some poor minor official, I could have befriended him long ago, and my life would not have been lived in vain. Though in station I am so much higher than he, all this brocade, embroidery, gauze, and silk does no more than wrap a piece of dead wood; all this fine wine and tender lamb does no more than fill a cesspit and muddy ditch. Who would have thought that the very words ‘wealth and rank’ should be so defiled by me!” Qin Zhong, for his part, saw Baoyu’s outstanding looks and uncommon bearing, together with his golden crown, embroidered clothes, proud maids, and lavishly dressed pages, and thought, “Now that I see Baoyu, it is no wonder everyone dotes on him. How hateful that I alone should have been born into a poor and humble family, unable to be constantly at his side! Truly, the word ‘poverty’ fetters a man and is one of the greatest miseries in this world.” Thus the two of them indulged in the same sort of wild imagining. Suddenly Baoyu asked Qin Zhong what books he was studying. When asked, Qin Zhong answered him truthfully. After they had exchanged a dozen or so remarks, each felt himself growing still closer to the other.

p.src: Presently tea and fruit were set out, and Baoyu said, “Neither of us drinks wine. Put the fruit on the little kang in the inner room, and we will sit in there so that we don’t disturb you.” The two of them therefore went into the inner room to take tea. While Qin-shi was seeing that wine and fruit were laid out for Xifeng, she hurried into the inner room and cautioned Baoyu, “Uncle Baoyu, if your nephew happens to say something ill-considered, please do it for my sake and pay no attention to him. He may be shy, but he is stubborn and contrary by nature, and he is not always very accommodating—that much is true.” Baoyu laughed. “Go along. I understand.” Qin-shi gave her brother another round of admonitions before finally returning to keep Xifeng company.

p.src: Presently, both Xifeng and Lady You sent someone to ask Baoyu, “What would you like to eat? Whatever you want can be fetched from outside, so just ask.” Baoyu merely acknowledged the message. With no thought for food or drink, he only asked Qin Zhong about his family circumstances of late. Qin Zhong said, “My tutor died of illness last year. My father is advanced in years and disabled, and his official duties are burdensome, so he has not yet considered engaging another tutor. For now, I do no more than review my old lessons at home. Besides, to make progress in one’s studies, one must have one or two kindred spirits as companions and discuss matters together regularly.” Before he had finished, Baoyu replied, “Exactly! We have a clan school where members of the family who cannot afford a tutor may study, and relatives of the boys are also allowed to attend with them. My own tutor went home last year, so my studies too have been neglected. My father intends to send me there for the time being to review my old books; when my tutor returns next year, we can each resume studying at home. My grandmother objected that, first, there were too many boys in the clan school and she feared we might all get into mischief and make matters worse; and second, I had been ill for several days. So the matter has been postponed for now. From what you say, your honored father is now worried about this very matter. Why not explain it to him when you return today and come to our humble school? I shall keep you company, and we shall both benefit. Would that not be an excellent thing?” Qin Zhong smiled. “The other day my father mentioned at home the question of engaging a tutor. He too said that the charity school here was a good one and had meant to consult our kinsman by marriage here about securing an introduction. But as everyone here has been so busy, he felt it improper to trouble you over such a trifling matter. If Uncle Bao truly thinks this humble nephew fit even to grind ink and wash inkstones beside you, why not bring it about at once? Neither of us would neglect his studies; we could meet and talk often, comfort our parents, and enjoy the pleasure of friendship. Would that not be splendid?” “Do not worry, do not worry,” said Baoyu. When we go back, we shall tell your brother-in-law and sister, as well as Second Sister-in-law Lian. When you return home today, report it to your honored father; I shall report it to Grandmother when I get back. There is no reason why it should not be settled promptly.” Thus the two settled their plan. By then it was time to light the lamps. They went out and watched the others play cards for a while longer. When the scores were reckoned, it turned out that Qin-shi and Lady You had lost and owed the others a feast with wine and entertainment; it was agreed that the feast would be held the day after next. Meanwhile, they ordered dinner to be served.

p.src: After dinner, as it had grown dark, Lady You said, “First send two of the boys to escort young Master Qin home.” The married maids passed the order outside, but after a long while Qin Zhong rose and took his leave. Lady You asked, “Who has been assigned to escort him?” The women replied, “They assigned Jiao Da outside, but as it happens, Jiao Da is drunk and has started cursing again.” Both Lady You and Qin-shi exclaimed, “Why on earth did they choose him again? With all those boys available, could they not have assigned any one of them? Why must they provoke him?” Xifeng said, “I am forever telling you that you are too soft. If you let the servants at home behave like this, what will become of the household?” Lady You sighed. “Surely you know what Jiao Da is like? Even the master ignores him, and your elder brother Zhen ignores him too. It is only because, when he was young, he followed the old lords on three or four military campaigns. He carried the old master out from a heap of corpses and saved his life. Though starving himself, he stole food for his master; and after two days without water, when he found half a bowlful he gave it to his master and drank horse urine himself. Relying on those services and old ties, he was treated with special regard while our ancestors were alive. Who would be willing to make things difficult for him now? Now he is old, has no concern for appearances, and does nothing but drink. Once drunk, there is no one he will not curse. I often tell the stewards not to give him any duties, but simply to treat him as though he were dead, and leave it at that. Yet today they have assigned him again.” Xifeng said, “Of course I know Jiao Da. It is you who have no resolve. With a man like that, why not simply send him away to some distant estate and be done with it?” Then she asked, “Are our carriages ready?” Everyone standing below replied, “Everything is ready and waiting.”

p.src: Xifeng rose and took her leave, walking hand in hand with Baoyu. Lady You and the others escorted them to the great hall, where lamps and candles blazed brilliantly and the young servants all stood waiting on the vermilion steps. Jiao Da, emboldened by Jia Zhen’s absence—and knowing that even if Jia Zhen were home, he could do little to him—felt freer still to give unrestrained vent to his feelings. Taking advantage of his drunkenness, he first cursed Lai Er, the chief steward, saying, “You are unfair! You bully the weak and cringe before the strong. Whenever there is a good assignment, you give it to someone else; but when someone must be escorted in the dead of night, you assign me. You heartless little bastard! You are nothing but a sham steward! Do you not realize that when old Master Jiao Da lifts his foot, it rises higher than your head? Twenty years ago, whom did old Master Jiao Da consider worth noticing? Still less would I notice a pack of mongrel little bastards like you!” Just as he was cursing with greatest relish, Jia Rong came out escorting Xifeng’s carriage. Jiao Da ignored everyone’s shouts to stop, and Jia Rong, unable to endure it any longer, cursed him twice and ordered the servants to tie him up. “When he sobers up tomorrow, ask him whether he still wants to court death!” Jiao Da had no regard whatever for Jia Rong. Instead, he shouted all the louder and called after him, “Brother Rong, do not put on your airs as master in front of Jiao Da. Never mind the likes of you—even your father and grandfather would not dare swagger before Jiao Da! Without Jiao Da, do you think you people could have become officials and enjoyed all this glory, wealth, and luxury? Your ancestors risked death nine times out of ten to win this estate, yet now, instead of repaying my kindness, you put on the airs of a master before me. If you say no more to me, I may let it pass; but say another word, and our red blades will go in and come out white!” From her carriage, Xifeng said to Jia Rong, “Why do you not get rid of this lawless creature at once? Is he not a menace if you keep him here? If our relatives and friends should hear of it, would they not laugh at a family like ours for having neither law nor discipline?” “Yes,” Jia Rong replied.

Jiao Da had no regard whatever for Jia Rong. Instead, he shouted all the louder and called after him, “Brother Rong, do not put on your airs as master in front of Jiao Da.
Never mind the likes of you—even your father and grandfather would not dare swagger before Jiao Da!
Without Jiao Da, do you think you people could have become officials and enjoyed all this glory, wealth, and luxury?
Your ancestors risked death nine times out of ten to win this estate, yet now, instead of repaying my kindness, you put on the airs of a master before me.
If you say no more to me, I may let it pass; but say another word, and our red blades will go in and come out white!”
From her carriage, Xifeng said to Jia Rong, “Why do you not get rid of this lawless creature at once?
Is he not a menace if you keep him here?
If our relatives and friends should hear of it, would they not laugh at a family like ours for having neither law nor discipline?”
“Yes,” Jia Rong replied.

p.src: Seeing that he had grown altogether too unruly, several of the young servants had no choice but to rush forward, wrestle him down, bind him, and drag him off to the stables. Jiao Da grew still more abusive, even bringing Jia Zhen into his tirade as he shouted wildly, “I am going to the ancestral hall to weep before the Old Master! Who could ever have imagined that such beasts as these would be born into the family by now! Day after day there is every kind of filthy mischief: some sleep with their daughters-in-law, others keep up affairs with their brothers-in-law. What is there that I do not know? But we must ‘hide a broken arm inside the sleeve’ and keep the family scandal to ourselves!” When the young servants heard him utter such unspeakable obscenities, they were terrified out of their wits. Caring for nothing else, they tied him up and crammed his mouth full of earth and horse dung.

p.src: Wang Xifeng, Jia Rong, and the others heard him from a distance, but all pretended they had heard nothing. Baoyu, watching this drunken commotion from the carriage, found it rather amusing and asked Wang Xifeng, “Cousin, you heard him say, ‘some sleep with their daughters-in-law.’ What does that mean?” At this, Wang Xifeng raised her brows, glared at him, and sharply rebuked him: “Do not talk such nonsense! That was nothing but filth spewed from a drunkard’s mouth. A boy of your standing ought to have pretended not to hear it, yet here you are asking for details!
